references.text: The Israelites cried out to the Lord for help when they were oppressed, and the Lord raised up a deliverer for them, following the same pattern as in the time of Gideon.
The Israelites cried out to the Lord, and he sent them a deliverer, a recurring pattern in Judges.
The Israelites cried out to the Lord for help during Jabin's oppression, parallel to their cry under the Midianite oppression.
The Israelites cried out to the Lord and confessed their sin, a situation similar to that in Gideon's time.
The Israelites groaned and cried out to God during slavery in Egypt, and God heard their cry, following the same pattern as in the period of the judges.
God heard Israel's cry and came down to deliver them from Egypt, prefiguring God's response to Israel's cries for help.
Samuel reminds the people that they cried out to the Lord when they were oppressed, and the Lord sent deliverers.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles, a universal principle of answered prayer.
Nehemiah describes how God heard the Israelites' cry and sent deliverers during the time of the judges.
